feedback: Approved. This candidate changes one controller field from the best raced design, iteration 3 (471.07): kd goes from 0.5 to 0.7, with base_speed 1.1, kp 1.6, ki 0, last_direction, and the iteration 3 geometry (x -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y 0.05, size 0.012) all unchanged. Iteration 4 showed that lowering speed to 1.0 did not help (445.98, oval 19/20), so returning to 1.1 is justified. Iteration 3 telemetry showed s-bend max_error at 0.0598 m with steering_oscillation 0.3087, and the oval at 20/20 with a 1.959 s mean finish, so the bend overshoot is the problem and damping is the natural lever. kd has not been isolated before: iteration 1 changed it together with speed, and iteration 2 changed it together with sensor geometry. The geometry must not change: the iteration 2 sensor-spacing and y 0.07 change scored 62.76 with 2.8 line-loss events on the oval. Nothing in the candidate is outside the contract, and it is a clean single-variable test of the best design, so it is worth racing. After the race, read the per-track results as follows. If the oval loses finishes or its steering_oscillation rises well above the iteration 3 value of 0.138, kd is too high for the straights, so return kd to 0.5 and test kp 1.4 next. If the s-bend and slalom still reach max_error at or above 0.06 m with kd 0.7, raise kd further, as the next single step.
requested_changes: If the oval loses finishes (below 20/20) or its steering_oscillation rises well above 0.138 (iteration 3), return controller.kd to 0.5 and test controller.kp at 1.4 with base_speed 1.1, since kd 0.5 kept the oval at 20/20.

If the s-bend or slalom still reach max_error at or above 0.06 m while the oval still finishes 20/20, raise controller.kd from 0.7 to 0.9, keeping base_speed at 1.1, because s-bend max_error has sat at 0.060 to 0.063 across speeds 1.3, 1.1 and 1.0.

Keep geometry.sensor_positions at the iteration 3 layout (x -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y 0.05). The iteration 2 change to 0.04 m spacing and y 0.07 scored 62.76 with 2.8 line-loss events on the oval, so do not reintroduce it.
